newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee ends firm on late dollar sales.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee ends firm on late dollar sales.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee rallied from the day's low to close a shade firmer on Friday after late selling of the dollar lifted the currency, dealers said.
The rupee closed at 58.38 to the dollar, after opening at 58.39 and slipping back to 58.43, they said.
"The rupee fell to 58.43 when speculators began buying dollars due to its overseas gains and the Central Bank's action," said a Seylan Bank dealer.
The Central Bank pushed up the dollar by two local cents and fixed buying and selling rates at 58.2739 and 59.4511.
"But last minute selling of dollars by a state bank pushed the rupee back up," said a Standard Chartered Bank dealer.
Dealers say the dollar should climb to around 58.75-58.80 rupees by th end of next week, due mainly to easing money market volatility.
"Volatile call rates served to keep the dollar down. But money market worries seem to be easing, which means the dollar should be back up," said the Standard Chartered dealer.
Overnight call money rates closed at 15 percent, after opening at 18.
Dealers said rupees, which had left the system due to quarterly tax payments and heavy cash calls following holidays in April and May, were returning to circulation.
The Central Bank buying treasury bills at Wednesday's auctions will also improve market liquidity, they said.
